status: PROPOSED — design input for M8 adoption (D-D, D-062 R3); not ratified; values TUNE
direction: Director 2026-10-24: switch government once its node is researched; advantages shown on the node; no policy cards — the Civ VI card slots are pre-chosen per government and built in.
law2: Every built-in policy is a coefficient inside a named resolution equation; none is a free-floating buff.
civ6Source: Civilization VI base ruleset Governments.xml (slot counts, bonus types)

switching.eligibility: The form's node is researched (which already requires every prerequisite). Research is permanent, so an eligible form stays eligible.
switching.order: AdoptGovernment(form) — one order, the same for player and AI (parity); validated at preview and delivery.
switching.firstAdoption: A polity starts under kin rule (no form). Its first adoption is immediate and costs nothing.
switching.cost: Each later switch costs Civics Points equal to 25 % of the new form's research cost (TUNE), paid on the turn the order is delivered; refused if the bank is short (nothing paid).
switching.transition: A transition of 2 sim-years plus 1 year for each class whose enfranchisement changes (TUNE): the old package is off, the new one not yet on, and tax extraction runs at half its rate. Integrated over dtYears, never counted in turns.
switching.cooldown: No new switch while a transition runs, and none within 10 sim-years of the last delivered switch (elapsed sim-time since the polity's own act — state, not a calendar gate).
switching.exchange: On the switch turn the RP<->CP exchange of cp-economy-proposal §3 may ride on the same order.
switching.resistance: Classes that lose enfranchisement gain grievance (NeedsGrievance, M9); until M9 this line is shown but has no effect.
switching.milestone: M8 (D-D, D-062 R3: adoption and active political effects are M8). Until then the node shows the package as 'available when government switching arrives'.
